# Default values for cue.
# This is a YAML-formatted file.
# Declare variables to be passed into your templates.

replicaCount: 1

sealedSecrets:
  enabled: false

image:
  registry: docker.io
  repository: cue
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  # Overrides the image tag whose default is the chart appVersion.
  tag: "latest"

# Global image settings for all services
global:
  imageRegistry: ""
  imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

# Backend services common configuration
backend:
  replicaCount: 1
  imageTag: latest
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 500m
    requests:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
  env: {}

# List of backend services
backendServices:
  - name: auth-service
    port: 8080
  - name: user-service
    port: 8080
  - name: profile-service
    port: 8080
  - name: discovery-service
    port: 8080
  - name: booking-service
    port: 8080
  - name: payment-service
    port: 8080
  - name: chat-service
    port: 8080
  - name: notification-service
    port: 8080
  - name: review-service
    port: 8080
  - name: support-service
    port: 8080
  - name: analytics-service
    port: 8080
  - name: api-gateway
    port: 8080

# Frontend configuration
frontend:
  imageTag: latest
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 500m
    requests:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m

# Infrastructure services
postgres:
  imageTag: "15.19"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 500m
    requests:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    # existingVolumeName:
    accessMode: ReadWriteOnce
    size: 10Gi

rabbitmq:
  imageTag: "3-management"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 500m
    requests:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m

redis:
  imageTag: "7-alpine"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

jaeger:
  imageTag: "1.47"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 1Gi
      cpu: 500m
    requests:
      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 250m

# Secret values (to be set by the user, preferably via --set-file or --set-string)
# RAW secrets (no base64 required)
# Example: echo -n "your-value" | base64
secret:
  # PostgreSQL credentials
  POSTGRES_USER: postgres
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
  POSTGRES_DB: cue_db

  # RabbitMQ credentials
  RABBITMQ_USER: admin
  RABBITMQ_PASSWORD: secret

  # Redis password
  REDIS_PASSWORD: secret

  # Stripe API key for payments
  STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: sk_test_421ffVAem5k5Ea8 # placeholder

  # JWT signing key for authentication tokens
  JWT_SIGNING_KEY: supersecretjwtskieforlocal # placeholder

  # Auth Service specific secrets
  JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES: "15"
  JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS: "7"

  # Database connection strings
  AUTH_DB_CONNECTION: Host=loveagain-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue_db;Username=postgres;Password=secret
  # Auth Service DB connection string
  USER_DB_CONNECTION: Host=loveagain-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue_db;Username=postgres;Password=secret
  # User Service DB connection string
  BOOKING_DB_CONNECTION: Host=loveagain-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue_db;Username=postgres;Password=secret
  # Booking Service DB connection string
  PAYMENT_DB_CONNECTION: Host=loveagain-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue_db;Username=postgres;Password=secret
  # Payment Service DB connection string
  # Connection string for AuthService (used by Entity Framework Core)
  ConnectionStrings__CueDatabase: Host=loveagain-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue_db;Username=postgres;Password=secret

  # Email service credentials (if using external email provider)
  EMAIL_API_KEY: c2vjcmV0 # placeholder
  EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS: cue@mailcompany.com

  # Redis connection strings
  REDIS_CONNECTION_STRING: redis://redis:6379

# Example of how to generate base64 values:
# Linux/macOS:  echo -n "your-value" | base64
# Windows PS:   [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes("your-value"))

# Ingress configuration
ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: ""
  annotations: {}
    # kubernetes.io/ingress.class: nginx
    # kubernetes.io/tls-acme: "true"
  hosts:
    - host: chart-example.local
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: ImplementationSpecific
        - path: /api
          pathType: ImplementationSpecific
  tls: []
  #  - secretName: chart-example-tls
  #    hosts:
  #      - chart-example.local

# Service configuration for all services (if needed)
service:
  type: ClusterIP
  port: 80

# Resource limits and requests can be overridden per service above, but we provide a default here.
resources: {}
  # We usually recommend not to specify default resources and to leave this as a conscious
  # choice for the user. This also increases chances charts run on environments with little
  # resources, such as Minikube. If you do want to specify resources, uncomment the following
  # lines, adjust them as necessary, and remove the curly braces after 'resources:'.
  # limits:

  #   cpu: 100m

# Tolerations for pod assignment.

tolerations: []

affinity: {}

file.content:
# Build stage
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci

# Copy source
COPY . .

# Build the app
RUN npm run build

# Production stage
FROM node:20-alpine

WORKDIR /app

# Install a lightweight HTTP server to serve the static build
RUN npm install -g serve

# Copy built artifacts from builder
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist

# Expose port
EXPOSE 3000

# Health check
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD node -e "require('http').get('http://localhost:3000', (r) => {if (r.statusCode !== 200) throw new Error(r.statusCode)})"

# Start the application
CMD ["serve", "-s", "dist", "-l", "3000"]

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src

COPY backend ./backend
COPY shared ./shared

WORKDIR /src/backend/Services/ProfileService
RUN dotnet restore ProfileService.csproj
RUN dotnet publish ProfileService.csproj -c Release -o /app/publish --no-restore

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 AS final
WORKDIR /app

ENV ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://+:8080
EXPOSE 8080

COPY --from=build /app/publish .

ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "ProfileService.dll"]

# Local deployment values for cue-platform Helm chart
# For deployment on a local k3s/minikube cluster

# Image registry and pull policy
image:
  registry: docker.io/library
  pullPolicy: Never  # Use local docker images, don't pull from registry
  tag: "latest"

# Global image settings
global:
  imageRegistry: 172.17.0.1:5000
  imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

# Backend services configuration
backend:
  replicaCount: 1
  imageTag: latest
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

# Frontend configuration
frontend:
  imageTag: latest
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

# PostgreSQL configuration
postgres:
  imageTag: "15-3.4"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    accessMode: ReadWriteOnce
    size: 5Gi

# RabbitMQ configuration
rabbitmq:
  imageTag: "3-management"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

# Redis configuration
redis:
  imageTag: "7-alpine"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m
    requests:
      memory: 64Mi
      cpu: 50m

# Jaeger configuration (distributed tracing)

The Helm upgrade failed with a **resource timeout** after5min because the deployments were still “InProgress” – none of the pods became Available within the timeout. The cause is mostly twofold:

1. **Image availability** – the chart pulls service images named, e.g., `cue-auth-service:latest`. * On the k3s cluster the container runtime (containerd) cannot see the Docker‑engine images you built locally, so the image pull fails and the pods never start. * The `postgres` image likewise is missing (ErrImageNeverPull) because `cue-cue-postgres:latest` was built locally but containerd doesn’t have it.

2. **Service startup errors** – most services crash on init, typically due to failing to connect to PostgreSQL (`Name or service not known`). The DB connection string in the secret uses the host `loveagain-cue-postgres-service`, but because the Postgres pod never starts, the connectivity check fails and the services immediately crash.

```bash#1. Run a registrydocker run -d -p5000:5000 --name registry registry:2#2. **Option B – load images directly into containerd**

If you prefer not to run a registry:

```bash# export each image as a tarball and load it into containerdfor img in $(docker images --format "{{.Repository}}"); do docker save $img:latest | ctr images import -
done```

After either method, verify that the images appear in `docker images` and in containerd (you can run `ctr image list`) on the node.

###2. Verify PostgreSQL starts correctlyThe Postgres pod (`cue-cue-postgres`) is still failing to start: you saw `ErrImageNeverPull`. Once the `postgres:15` image exists in the registry or local store, the pod should pull it and start. Check the pod logs:

```bashkubectl logs -n cue-platform -f cue-cue-postgres-6b8d8865d7-7wfwx```

You should see normal PostgreSQL startup logs.

###3. Let the services startWhen Postgres is up, the back‑end services will be able to connect and will stop crashing.

```bashkubectl rollout status deployment -n cue-platform --watch```

If all services become **Available:1/1**, the Helm release will complete successfully.

###4. Re‑run the Helm upgrade with a generous timeout```bashhelm upgrade --install cue ./helm-chart \
 -n cue-platform \
 -f helm-chart/values-local.yaml \
 --wait --timeout10m```

The `--wait` flag makes Helm pause until all pods are ready; the10min timeout should be ample.

### Why the Postgres pod is in `ErrImageNeverPull` - **`imagePullPolicy: Never`** – the template sets `imagePullPolicy` to whatever you put in `global.imagePullPolicy`.- In your *local values file* you set ```yaml global: imageRegistry: "" imagePullPolicy: Never ``` so Helm tells Kubernetes “never pull this image”; it must already exist in the container runtime. - Because the image **`postgres:15`** has never been pushed to the cluster’s container runtime (containerd), the pod cannot start and Kubernetes reports **`ErrImageNeverPull`**. All the other services show `ImagePullBackOff` for the same reason – Kubernetes tries to pull `auth-service:latest`, `user-service:latest`, … and cannot find them locally either. --- ## Two ways to fix it| Option | What you get | How to keep it running | |--------|--------------|------------------------| | **A. Use a local registry (recommended for dev)** | You continue to *push* images with Docker, and the cluster pulls them from you. |
  • Start a registry (`docker run -d -p5000:5000 --name registry registry:2`).
  • Tag each service image to that registry.
  • Push the images there.
  • Set `global.imageRegistry: localhost:5000` and `global.imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` in `values-local.yaml` (so the pod will pull from the registry if needed).
  • Leave the postgres image as `postgres:15` – Kubernetes will pull it from DockerHub automatically.
| | **B. Load images into containerd (no registry)** | No external registry is required. |
  • Leave `global.imageRegistry` empty.
  • Change `global.imagePullPolicy` to `Never` (or skip it to keep default).
  • For each image, `docker save … | ctr images import -` (once per image).
| Below are step‑by‑step commands for **Option A** – the one that keeps the chart unchanged and works on any Kubernetes (minikube, k3s, etc.). --- ##1️⃣ Push your locally built images to a registry```bash#1️⃣ start a registry (runs on port5000) docker run -d -p5000:5000 --restart=always --name registry registry:2#2️⃣ Tag and push every service image you built# (folder has them all under the repo names from your build script) for svc in auth-service user-service booking-service chat-service discovery-service notification-service payment-service profile-service review-service support-service analytics-service ; do docker tag $svc:latest localhost:5000/$svc:latest docker push localhost:5000/$svc:latestdone#3️⃣ OPTIONAL – push the postgres image too (just in case someone wants to pull it from your registry) docker tag postgres:15 localhost:5000/postgres:15docker push localhost:5000/postgres:15``` > **Tip** – after this you can verify the registry list: ```bashdocker run --rm --entrypoint="curl" registry:2127.0.0.1:5000/v2/_catalog# you should see: {"repositories":["auth-service","user-service", ...,"postgres"]} ``` --- ##2️⃣ Update your local values fileEdit `helm-chart/values-local.yaml` so that the chart will use the local registry for every service **and** allow image pulls when necessary: ```yamlglobal: imageRegistry: localhost:5000 # <--- tells the chart to prepend this imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent # <--- will pull from the registry if not present``` > Leave the `postgres` section as it is – the chart hard‑codes `postgres:{{ .Values.postgres.imageTag }}`.> With `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` the `postgres:15` image will be fetched from DockerHub (or your local registry if you pushed it). If you already have a `values-local.yaml` that contains `imagePullPolicy: Never`, just replace that line with the one above. --- ##3️⃣ Re‑install the chart cleanly```bash#1️⃣ remove the last half‑finished release (in case anything remains) helm uninstall cue -n cue-platform || true#2️⃣ delete the namespace so Helm can claim itkubectl delete namespace cue-platform --ignore-not-found=true#3️⃣ reinstall (Helm will create the namespace during the run) helm install cue ./helm-chart \ -n cue-platform \ -f helm-chart/values-local.yaml \ --create-namespace \ --wait --timeout15m``` If everything goes well, you should see output like: ```textNAME: cueLAST DEPLOYED: Thu Sep410:57:512026NAMESPACE: cue-platformSTATUS: deployed``` and the pods will switch to **Running**. --- ##4️⃣ Verify```bash# All pods are readykubectl get pods -n cue-platform# Check Postgres specificallykubectl logs -n cue-platform -f cue-cue-postgres-6b8d8865d7-7wfwx``` You should no longer see **`ErrImageNeverPull`** or **`ImagePullBackOff`** messages. --- ##5️⃣ What if you prefer *OptionB* (loading images into containerd)? If you *really* want to keep `imagePullPolicy: Never` and avoid an external registry, simply load the images into containerd once: ```bash# for every service image you builtfor svc in $(docker images --format "{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}" | grep :latest); do docker save $svc | ctr images import -done# do the same for postgresdocker save postgres:15 | ctr images import - ``` After that, `helm install …` will succeed even with `imagePullPolicy: Never`. --- ## TL;DR- `ErrImageNeverPull` means the image is not in the node’s container runtime.- Push the images you built to a registry **or** load them into containerd.- Set `global.imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` (or leave default).- Re‑install with `helm install … --wait`.- Check the pods – they should all become `Running`. Let me know if you hit any hiccups during the push or if the pod logs still report connection errors, and I’ll help you sort them out!
